Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from Acme InfoSec before we lock the deep-dive: 

1) SOC 2: can you confirm whether this is a SOC 2 Type II in progress or Type I? We need a projected completion date for our compliance board.
2) Log fields: please confirm that each API/admin log includes: principal identity (email/ID), action, timestamp (ISO8601), resource identifier, request id/correlation id, IP, and response code. An example JSON log would be ideal.
3) Immutability: does Redwood support exporting logs into an S3 bucket with object lock / WORM? If not, what is your recommended pattern for a tamper-evident archive?
4) Access: how will we control which Acme users can pull logs? We need RBAC mapped to our SSO.

If you can answer these at a high level here that would be great; we can cover details on the tech call.

Hi Tom / Lisa —

Appreciate the questions — below are concise answers and the patterns other enterprise customers use. Happy to walk through live and share example log payloads.

SOC 2 status
- We are currently undergoing SOC 2 Type II testing. Control testing began April 2026; the expected completion and final report delivery is targeted for 2026-07-15. We can share the final report when it is issued and in the meantime provide our SOC 2 readiness checklist and control mapping.

Log coverage & schema (high level)
- Admin activity logs: captures console actions and admin API events (actor, org, action, target resource, timestamp, outcome, request_id).
- API request logs: captures request_id, principal (user_id/email/service-account), endpoint, request method, payload hash, response_code, latency_ms, client_ip, region.
- Runtime/agent logs: model invocation ids, model_version, prompt_id, token counts, and error traces.

Example fields (we will provide JSON examples in the follow-up):
- timestamp, request_id, principal, principal_type, action, resource, outcome, client_ip, user_agent, latency_ms, error_code (if any), region

Exportability & immutability
- Export options: 1) Continuous streaming to your ingestion (AWS Kinesis / AWS Firehose) or GCP Pub/Sub; 2) Periodic batched exports to a customer-owned S3 bucket.
- Immutability: for batched S3 exports we support HMAC-signed manifests and checksums on each object; we can also write to customer S3 with Object Lock enabled for WORM compliance when Acme enables Object Lock on your side.
- Tamper-evidence: exports include signed manifests + per-object checksums and a signed index file we publish. For an additional layer, we can push cryptographic hashes to your internal verification service.

Retention & archival
- Retention is configurable per-account. Default retention for audit logs is 90 days in hot storage; archived exports can be retained long-term (we support retention policies up to 7 years or longer per contract).

Access controls & RBAC
- Logs are accessible through the Audit Logs API and via the Console for users with the "audit_reader" role. RBAC is integrated with SSO (SAML/OIDC). You can map Acme groups to roles; we support attribute-based access for finer controls.

HIPAA / GDPR notes
- GDPR: We provide DPA and data residency options (EU region deployments).
- HIPAA: We support HIPAA workloads under a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments; we can discuss coverage for hosted contracts during procurement.

SLA & availability
- Audit Log delivery for streaming exports is included in our Dedicated plans with 99.9% delivery SLA; batched exports are scheduled and retried with delivery guarantees documented in the export policy.

Attachments / next steps
- Attaching the SOC2-readiness-checklist.xlsx and will drop example JSON log payloads to the Drive link Marissa shared.
- If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive (I can walk your infra team through sample logs, set up a test streaming export to a sandbox S3, and validate retention/object-lock behavior).

Thanks —
